objective: The frontend works and passes lint, typecheck and every test on React 18 with eslint-plugin-react-hooks 5 and on React 19 with react-hooks 7 (and eslint 10), and the bundle budget accepts React 19's entry growth as a declared dependency major under ADR 0041 (brief.md quotes it), after the cheap trim, so Renovate's react monorepo and eslint 10 PRs can merge unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: the Director PR that folded FRONTEND-046 into BASE on main a777aae (vite 8) and added ADR 0041 has merged. No other PR that changes frontend/ is open. The branch is cut from a main that holds it.

Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation. They fail today because combine refuses a unit's entry growth over 1 kB gzip and clamps the entry at 480 kB raw, and FRONTEND-047.ts declares React 19's growth as a dependency major. The test commit also holds every test-file change the unit needs (allow_test_edits_during_impl is false), including the two react-hooks 7 errors that are in test files.

bundle-budget.ts: UnitBudget gains an optional dependencyMajor: { name: string; decision: string }. combine accepts entryJsGzipGrowth over ENTRY_GROWTH_PER_UNIT_MAX only from a unit that declares it, with a non-empty name and a decision matching /^ADR \d{4}$/; any other unit still throws. The entry raw ceiling is min(BASE raw + tolerance + every unit's raw growth, ENTRY_JS_RAW_HARD_MAX + the raw growth of the dependency-major units). bundle-budget-combine.test.ts pins: growth past 1 kB accepted with dependencyMajor, refused without it or with a malformed decision, and the raw cap lifted by exactly the major's raw growth and no more.

The 16 react-hooks 7 errors are fixed in the code, not suppressed: no eslint-disable comment for a react-hooks rule, and eslint.config.js unchanged. Sites on main a777aae: refs, AttachmentPicker.tsx:53 (2), 54, 55, 56 (2), 85 (2), useCardReady.ts:143, StatsNavigator.tsx:201; set-state-in-effect, AuthContext.tsx:58, MediaWidget.tsx:174, AppLayout.tsx:199; immutability, TeamLevel.tsx:271; globals, AuthContext.test.tsx:36 and src/test/render.test.tsx:35. Every fix uses only APIs that exist in React 18 (no useEffectEvent, no use, no ref-as-prop), and behaviour is unchanged.

Each production site's current behaviour is pinned by a test before it changes: where no existing test covers the behaviour a fix touches (a reset on prop change, a status during sign-in, a deletion-finished flag, a ready signal, a wins count), the test commit adds one, and it passes on today's code.

The cheap trim (ADR 0041): routes.tsx loads SearchPage lazily, as the other page routes are, unless doing so takes less than 1 kB gzip out of the entry on React 19; then it stays eager and the PR says so with the measurement. No other route moves: the thread modals and ComposeModal are on the home path (the composer is already lazy inside ComposeModal).

frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-047.ts declares, in the test commit: dependencyMajor { name: 'react 19', decision: 'ADR 0041' }; entryJsGzipGrowth and entryJsRawGrowth equal to the React 19 entry after the trim minus BASE (149,210 gzip, 474,565 raw), plus at most 1% of that entry each, rounded up to 100 B; and any lazy output the trim adds, with its measurement plus headroom. Its comment gives every measurement on both versions. Without the trim the probe measured 172,561 gzip and 554,083 raw (+23,351 and +79,518). No lazy output moves past tolerance on React 19 against this BASE (largest +38 B), so nothing else is declared.
